plan: In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding can yield negative profit if you win and pay more than your value; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive surplus. There’s only 1 round, so no signaling or learning. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value ($21). If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (≤21); if others bid higher than 21, I lose and pay nothing.

[ This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: underbidding risks losing when I would profit; overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds my value. Rational opponents likely follow the same rule. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round, I will bid my exact value of 22.0. ]

[ This is a standard second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational bidders. The dominant strategy is to bid one’s true value: bidding your value ensures you win exactly when your value exceeds the others’ and you pay the second-highest bid. Shading risks losing profitable wins without reducing the price when you still win. There’s only 1 round, so no dynamic considerations apply. Values are uniform 0–49; our value is 13, which is relatively low, so we likely lose, but truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. Bid in 0.1 increments; 13 is valid. ]
